question: Should OpenClaw standardize the proposed 12-line-or-700-UTF-16-unit collapse rule for long user messages across the web, iOS, and Android chat clients?
rationale: This is a new visible cross-client interaction contract rather than a repair of an established broken behavior; the protected maintainer label requires explicit human product acceptance.

options.title: Adopt the shared disclosure policy
options.body: Accept the 12-line/700-unit rule and review the branch for normal landing after confirming the intended cross-client interaction contract.

options.title: Adjust the product threshold or scope
options.body: Keep the disclosure concept but request a revised threshold, client scope, or persistence behavior before approving the implementation.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the current transcript rendering until a maintainer sponsors a narrower chat-readability direction.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared disclosure policy
recommendation.body: Accept the 12-line/700-unit rule and review the branch for normal landing after confirming the intended cross-client interaction contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence ties steipete to the complete cross-platform implementation, although broader feature-history ownership could not be independently established.
